accent.name: Accent
accent.summary: The way a speaker pronounces a language. An accent concerns pronunciation only.

act-of-union.name: Act of Union
act-of-union.summary: Under the Act of Union, the formation of Great Britain with the unification of England and Wales with Scotland.

competence.name: Competence
competence.summary: A speaker's underlying knowledge of their language, as opposed to how they use it.

dialect.name: Dialect
dialect.summary: A variety of a language that differs in vocabulary and grammar as well as pronunciation, linked to a region or a social group.

edwardian-era.name: Edwardian era
edwardian-era.summary: A British Civilization in Transition, and a period when British imperial power was evolving.

noam-chomsky.name: Noam Chomsky
noam-chomsky.summary: American linguist, philosopher and cognitive scientist, known for generative grammar and Universal Grammar.

image.alt: Noam Chomsky in a video call: an older man with white hair and a white beard, in front of a wall of bookshelves.

norbert-elias.name: Norbert Elias
norbert-elias.summary: Found that civilization describes a process that refers to something which is constantly in motion and is constantly moving forward.

performance.name: Performance
performance.summary: How language is actually used in real situations, with its pauses, slips and restarts.

william-labov.name: William Labov
william-labov.summary: American linguist (1927 to 2024) and a pioneer of variationist sociolinguistics. He studied the dialects and accents of New York.

image.alt: William Labov, an older man with glasses and a light brown jacket, resting his chin on his hand and looking to the side.
